text: Please read my experience and use another mover... Thank me later... My family recently moved from NOLA to another state and found Lee moving online. One of their associates came to our small apartment and met with my husband to give us an estimate for a full pack with an additional pickup from a local storage facility. She seemed knowledgeable so we decided to use them for our move. Packing day: The movers showed up bright and early. They came in and took one look and their enthusiasm immediately faded. They stated that they were unaware it was a full pack, that we had so much stuff and that they were unsure if they even had enough boxes. ??? They had to call in one additional guy to help pack. The team had no power drills to take down the beds and toddler beds so they had to use manual tools (not sure why). Several times during the day the team took smoke breaks as their enthusiasm began to fade even more. Granted, it was hot outside but it seemed excessive to us. My mild mannered physician husband berated them for so many breaks and even called our moving contact at Lee moving to complain - to little avail. We also had some boxes and other items in a local storage facility that needed to be moved as well. Since the team at our apartment was super slow, another crew of two was called in to get our boxes from storage. Unpacking day: A different team of two delivered our items - they were very friendly and showed up early. It started to rain during the process - my husband (not the movers) had to go outside to close the truck so our goods would not get wet. Immediately after the unpacking, I called Lee moving to let them know that our carpet was slightly damaged during the unpacking. I received an email the next day that it would be covered with information on how to process a claim. I decided to check the items in all of the boxes before submitting a claim about a week later. It's during these days that I noticed a nice puncture hole in the top of an armoire as well as a broken candleholder. I took pictures and submitted one claim for all three issues. I reached out to my assigned claims agent to ask the status. She responded via email that I would receive a check for the armoire and candleholder ONLY. I was told to contact Lee moving regarding the damaged carpet. I spoke with the manager on 2 occasions. He stated that he would kindly call me back after he had time to research my inquiry/claim. I received an email that they do not clean carpet - he never called me back. NOTE: The claim was not for the carpet to be cleaned.... My multiple calls to Lee moving has gone ignored. We spent $7k with this company and are being mistreated after trusting our personal items to them for safe transport and delivery. I subsequently filed a complaint with the BBB of Greater New Orleans. The company responded that protection was placed on floors (it was not) and that a final walk through was done (it was not). Bottom line: No one treats your items like you do. Please do yourself a favor and use another mover... Thank me later..

text: I visited this location late on a Sunday night when the Wife and Daughter couldn't wait to get home to eat. We chose Chili's specifically because of their relatively late Sunday night closing time of 11pm. It's only 10pm in Gallatin, e.g. The restaurant was abandoned and only a few drunks remained at the bar. Only bar seating was available, which was fine. Two young ladies took turns waiting on us as they closed down the restaurant. The service was good, considering it had likely already been a long day for staff. We got the white spinach queso which is always great. The girls drank water and I tried the merlot, which was very fruit, and the cabernet, which was much better. The disappointment came with the entree the girls ordered to share. The chicken fingers came in a deep-fried, tempura type batter. It was not bad, per se, it was just odd. It was a little dense, even if it had otherwise seemed appropriate. The fries were only so-so, and the broccoli was raw-not even steamed. The whole thing was kind of off, and if you're thinking, "Well, that's what you should expect on a Sunday night at 10pm", you're right. I did expect that. But I hoped for better. I'm old school and so I think if you're going to claim to remain open until 11, which, let's face it, is not really that late, even for Hendersonville, then you should be in a ready to serve posture. If you don't want to serve that late, then close earlier, and change your hours. But doing things half-assed, just because that's what works most of the time for most people in this country, is a real disappointment. The girls were polite, but didn't hide the fact they wanted us gone. They didn't even address it forthright, as you might expect, by saying, "It's 10pm and no one else is here so we're going to start shutting down the kitchen...", it was just unspoken. I tipped 20% as I always do unless service is horrible, because this is a tough job, but I wasn't thrilled. If it seems that I'm a cranky old man, well, I am 40 and I am generally disappointed by the mediocrity that is common in our culture. I want and hope for best. I hope my experience at this Chili's is unusual.
label: NEG

text: My man and I had so much fun on our spooky date night at Creamy Acres last Friday! We arrived around 8pm and the lines for tickets were super long. Luckily, we had purchased ours in advance so the line for pre-purchased tickets was much shorter. There are two ways to go once you have your tickets: get in line for one of two haunted houses or get in line for the haunted hayride, which actually leads you through two or three other attractions once you are off the hayride. We were encouraged to check out the haunted house first, so we got in line for the one on the left. The line took about 20 minutes or so, but the haunted house was pretty awesome. It took longer to walk through than I expected, or maybe it just felt that way because I was terrified and couldn't wait to get out of it! Next up was the hayride, which was a significantly longer wait time. We probably waited for about 45 minutes to finally board the ride. I was extremely impressed with the ride - for a farm in South Jersey, they really had some amazing special effects and set designs. Totally worth the wait, especially considering the fact that the ride was followed up with a haunted corn maze (which me managed to escape from quickly) and another haunted house, plus a strange but cool haunted rain forest type thing. After all of the screaming, we stopped by the snack bar and enjoyed hot apple cider and a pumpkin donut - just $1 each! VIP tickets allow you to skip the lines but they cost twice as much as regular tickets. My advice would be to go on a weeknight, if possible, to avoid long waits in line. Great night out and would definitely go again.

text: Ate at his truck during GenCon this year. I will not buy from them again. The short version: I was unimpressed due to the long wait time (35+ minutes), lackluster food (had the BBQ Chicken Cone with regular FF), small portion size compared to the price ($9.45 for a small entree and small fry), an incorrect order, and poor customer service (see below for details). The experience: I was between events and looking for lunch, and the Scratch truck offered selections that looked great on the menu. This, combined with the high review average on Yelp and the seemingly short line, had me excited to try their food. The line in front of me consisted of 8 or 9 parties. Most of them were single orders, but 2 of them had multiple entrees. My entire wait time between entering the line and getting my food was about 35 minutes, which was an exorbitant amount of time compared to other trucks that had showed up for the event. Two of my friends were able to get through comparatively sized lines at other trucks and had finished eating their meals before I even received my food. Once at the window I ordered the BBQ Chicken Cone with regular french fries. I asked if I could pay for extra chicken in the cone, but was told that they could not because the tortilla was already stuffed to capacity. I later found out that this was not true, but I'll get to the food in a moment. Since I could not get extra chicken I asked for extra fries. At this point they tried to up-sell me on their spicy fries, which I wasn't interested in. I confirmed my previous request for a double order of regular fries, to which the order taker responded she had added. The listed price was $8.75, and I was charged $9.45. I assumed, incorrectly, this was the up-charge for the fries. I later found out it was a separate tax charge. After waiting for 35 minutes (and watching several people who ordered after me receive their food first, possibly because the chicken takes longer to cook??) I received a chicken cone that was not nearly as full as I was led to believe, and a single order of fries. I stated to the gentleman who handed me my food that I had asked for extra fries, to which his response was to wave the receipt in my face and tell me that I had only asked for a single order. At this point my patience had reached my limit, and I am ashamed to admit that I made a crude comment. After I snapped he seemed to want to make things correct, but by this time I wanted nothing more to do with the truck, so I walked away. The food: When I started eating I found there was plenty of space left in my tortilla and my last few bites actually consisted of nothing but BBQ sauce and tortilla. The chicken was tough and chewy, and was completely drowned in BBQ sauce. I found the fries to be a little under cooked for my taste, but they would be fine for anyone who likes steak fries and they were very well seasoned. I had considered ordering the special of the day, which was a grilled cheese on Texas toast with pulled pork on it, and now I wish I had. The BBQ chicken cone was underwhelming at best, and the meal left me still hungry. The portion size and food quality were definitely not worth the price. Notes to the vendor: If you end up reading this review, I would like to apologize for losing my temper. I would mention, however, that when a customer reports a problem with their order the correct response is not, and never will be, blaming the problem on said customer. This would have been a 3 star review had it not been for the poor response to my complaint. Also, consider incorporating tax into the listed menu pricing for convenience. Of the 4 food trucks I ate from during this convention, yours was the only one that separately charged tax.
label: NEG

text: I can be so annoying sometimes... so irrational. The more I think about it, the less I understand how this just happened. I called That's Amore! to order a pepperoni pizza for the Finicky Eater who was starving madly as he returned from four hours of rowing. I recall using my cell phone. I recall a very feminine voice answering very sweetly. I recall me saying: "I don't have the number of the pizza part of your restaurant. Can I order one through you?" I remember her saying: "of course! Give me a second." Then as I sat watching the oranges and the cotton candy pinks of the sunset color the sky, I listened... and listened... and listened as people were greeted, seated, the jazz musician finished his set... Then I whispered a couple of "hellos" into the void of nothingness. I said some "hola! Hola!"... and I eventually screamed a couple, or many many more times, "Are you kidding me-s?" After exactly ten minutes, because I am impatient that way... I grabbed my silver purse, prayed to the angel of elevators not to disconnect the call, and cat walked myself many stories down, into and out of lobbies, across cobblestone streets and, like a Puerto Rican tropical storm... holding the same bejeweled cased phone, sashayed into the quite empty restaurant. A very beautiful girl greeted me. Yes. A very stunning girl who sounded just like the one who I needed to keep conversing with welcomed me. She did not get me when I said: "please, pick up the phone and let me finish my order." She, so beautifully, thought I was speaking to someone else. Yes. I guess I was being rude walking into the restaurant in full conversation with someone else. Because I am rude like that. I proceeded to very calmly, not to hold in my wrath, No.... but to make myself very clear, explained that I was still speaking to her on the overlooked and long forgotten black artifact she claimed had been defective throughout the day... No apologies. I firmly walked to the pizza bar as she beautifully followed me. The Pizza chef joyfully asked me how I was doing. I take responsibility for answering with a flat "I have being better." He repeated it as if in disbelief "she has being better..." Beautiful whispered something about the phone, which he promptly took and placed back in its receptor "to charge it." He diligently placed the frozen crust on the silver tray and in seconds had the pizza shoved in the hot oven... secretly hoping to lower the temperature around us which had risen higher than in there. I begged her to charge me and handed her my credit card. Chef returned to the register to explain to Lovely how to do it. She handed me the receipt. I asked for a pen. I signed. She kept her credit card on my hand and I asked for it back. Got it. Grabbed the square. Left the place... and her as she was ogled by two very old men.

text: As a Brazilian, used to having a Churrascaria at every corner of my neighborhood, this place was a disappointment. Not the staff... the staff was fantastic. Really good people, but what we got for our money was terrible. I took a bunch of my co-workers touting all of the different cuts and showing them pictures from their website and from yelp and everyone was very excited. The salad and hot bar was very limited, missing several of the typical Brazilian items, like hearts of palm, cubed cheeses, tropero beans etc. But we don't care as long as the meat is good, and that's where this place failed. Terribly. It was an endless rotation of Michingan steak (very cheap meat), top sirloin (Picanha - this was the best part), an odd cut of chicken and Calabresa Sausage (which is much better than any other sausage sold in the US). Everything else on their menu, we had to ask them to make. They offered brisket as a replacement for Cupin(A very fatty and tender cut) and a Set of barbecue ribs that I could stop and get one better at any gas station BBQ joint. The ribs were not even close to being Brazilian style and weren't even the same animal. We asked to filet wrapped in bacon, we got something swimming in garlic that we couldn't taste the mean. We asked for chicken hearts, and when it came out, 3 people of my group decided to try them. The chicken hearts were RAW. So much so that, although this is my favorite, i had to spit it out. At the end of the night, we separated the bills. I was charged for 1 meal, + 3 guarana cans (soda) + 2 deserts(to take home for my wife since she does not eat meat) My bill was $66.xx , and for that price, one would expect perfection. Ahhh, and one more thing. The deserts were 3 leches cake, which, according to my wife, Walmart makes it better and a Pudim (Brazilian flan with plum sauce), which was bland, dry and overcooked. (Plum Sauce was good thou) There are better Churrascarias in Orlando, for half the price, if you're willing to drive for 45 minutes, and if you really want good food, i suggest you do. Sorry, i really wanted this place to be good. maybe it was an off night.
label: NEG

text: This area off Shell point Rd., is over a small bridge, which makes it a private Islad. The island is man made and all composed of fill. Years latter the original few condos, 2 houses,a marina, a motel & eventually a restaurant appeared. Now that Little harbour has taken over, they have overpopulated the island & ruined the totally unique quaint & exclusiveness of this area. The hotel was redone & all rooms are 2 room suites. Personally I grew up with this area in my life & even lived there, at 1 point in time. Even though I am disquested with what Little Harbour has done to the island, I still use it as a private get away at times. Most of the individual hotel suites have been sold as condos. The beach is across the street, very close, watch sunset from your living room or go to the Tiki bar. All of the rooms are pretty equal, price is usually not too high, 2 pools & relaxed environment. I know I am a bit partial, but I always enjoy my time here. If you are there on a weekend, chances are there will be at least 1 wedding on the beach.

text: This restaurant is in the space once occupied by Sofia's. It is intimate and cozy, the main dining room seats less than 20 and the bar area maybe 8 more. They have a custom cocktail list like so many great restaurants, and this one is reminiscent of the Franklin Mortgage and Investment Co., with its emphasis on brown liquids in all sorts of interesting combinations. The service was excellent, and personalized, she knew what to do and say for each customer. On to the food which was very protein-heavy, which I like. Then again, I like everything. I started with the beef tartare. The texture was very unctuous, soft and almost pudding-like. It felt wonderful on the mouth. Hints of mustard, citrus, perfectly seasoned but not overpowered. Some chefs feel the need to disguise the beef, not here. The accompanying bread slices were toasted with just a hint of cheese, again quite subtle, and there was a schmeer of a parsley-like very green puree that you could dip into as you wished. Very good! Just one note, there was too much bread so I didn't finish it. The second course was a special veal cheeks with sweetbreads. The meats were cooked perfectly, and the sauce, while quite rich and strong, was beautiful. The cheeks were even more tender than a falling-apart short rib. The main course was rabbit "pot-au-feu", I put that in parentheses because every pot-au-feu I have had has been much simpler and not very interesting. This dish was a complex mix of flavors, colors and textures, and included carrots and potatoes and a crostini with liver on it that complimented each bite fantastically. The sauce again was rich and soft. Coaxed to have dessert, I noted only three on the menu, all simple. I had the creme brûlée and it was what I consider perfect, which is to say that the texture was just slightly thinner than pudding. Creme brûlée should not be custardy or eggy, I think. Real vanilla beans of course, great caramelized crust. Bibou is the top feminine French bistro in Philly with its more delicate treatments of food, and I think Townsend must be the top masculine one. A bold menu that screams protein. Arrhh! Yum.

text: Beware of this restaurant: We went in as a party of 7 with empty stomachs and high hopes as the front door's "Zagat rated" signs assured me that the food was going to be excellent. The food itself, however, turned out to be average at best. Coming from an authentic Chinese family, and having been to many restaurants in China, the mediocre-level food did not fully satisfy my tastebuds, nor did it fill up my stomach. Being a Dim Sum-style restaurant, the food is all prepared and laid on carts. The waiters then push the carts around to different tables and you get to chose what dishes you want. The pro of this is that you can begin eating immediately, as the food is already prepared for you. However, some dishes were only warm, or slightly cold, which probably meant that the food has been on the cart for a while. This inevitably leads to a sub-par food experience, because hey, who wants to eat something that has been rolling around in a cart for 30 minutes? All in all, there were a few tasty dishes, but when looking at the meal overall, I give the quality of the food 3 stars. Now, moving onto why this restaurant got the rating it did in my view. Fundamentally, the goal of any restaurant should be to satisfy their customers, and therefore, customer service should be one of their top priorities. This is precisely the quality that this restaurant lacks. After we all finished our meals, we calculated our own bill before handing it over to the front desk and having them give us the bill. When we got our bill back, their calculation was around $15 MORE than what we calculated ourselves. Although this could have been an error on our part, that much of a difference for a ~$60 bill should not occur. We went up and told them about the discrepancy, and we ended up getting a measly $2 off our bill. Disappointedly, we left a small tip and proceeded to leave the table. As the servers began to clean the table, they noticed that we gave a below average tip and began to stop us from leaving. For obvious reasons, we left a small tip due to the fact that they had poor service overall and how they overcharged us for the food. The fact that we left them a tip at all should have exemplified our courtesy. However, they continued to argue with us, almost shouting, that we did not leave a big enough tip. Although the other people eating began to look up at the commotion, they had no shame and continued to insist how "we can't do this to them". At one point, they even asked US to clean the table for them. May I ask, is this the kind of service that you want as a customer going into your restaurant? Out of all the restaurants in Chinatown, we chose YOURS to come to, and this is the kind of service that we get? Tip is something that is optional, and not required by law. However, they acted in a manner as if we didn't pay the bill at all. We paid the bill in its entirety and the only thing that was off was the tip. Eventually, we had to force ourselves out of the restaurant, walking out in shame as they continued to yell at us. This was by far the worst experience I've had in a restaurant in my entire life. I know that I will personally not be coming nor recommending this restaurant to anyone in the future. Thanks a lot for reading this review, and I hope you have a nice day! :)

text: This was our 3rd and last time here. First of all, we moved from Hawaii to Reno recently, so we've eaten at various L&Ls arcross Hawaii. When in Hawaii, you can pretty much expect that each franchised location will cook and prepare in similar fashion, which means food tastes almost identical no matter which location you chose. I understand that with different regions, ingredient quality and supply will vary, so taste may be slightly affected. I can accept that. The previous 2 times here, I was not impressed. But since we really wanted to love the L&L in the area we now call home, Reno, we kept saying to give it another try. It was nice thinking we could still have a little comfort food that we are accustomed to from "back home", in Hawaii. So here's how our final visit went... We walked in to a pretty empty restaurant. There we're maybe 2 groups already sitting and eating their food. We we're greeted by a friendly (local) girl at the counter. Our group of 4 stand and stare at the menu for a few minutes. In those few minutes, we witness a very unsettling incident...a customer brings his food to the counter to tell the girl that he found a metal shard in his food (they figured it to be the metal from a brillo-like scrubber). The cashier doesn't hesitate at all, she quickly handles the situation. Stating she will have the cook prepare a new fresh plate. She sends the order back to the cook, who begins stating he can't cook a new meal without an order reciept(?). Immediately another female comes out from the back area, asking the cashier if there is a way to print a new order receipt. This goes back and forth as discussion between the two girls for a minute. Finally, its resolved, however, when the female returns to the back area, the cook angrily speaks to her, in a tone loud enough for us customers in the front to overhear. It made me think about leaving, but the rest of my party wanted to stay and eat. So, we proceed to order our food. Okay, no biggie, we sit down and patiently wait for our food. While waiting, we see the female employee who the cooked just got finishing yelling at, walking outside...I felt so bad for her, in my opinion, she did nothing wrong, except attempt to correct an order for a customer. She was a champ! She maintained her composure, cooled off, and then went back to helping customers. Now here's the kicker!! Our food finally arrives, we eagerly open our plate lunches, anticipating some ono food. Bah humbug! My pork tocino, can't tell if it's raw or cooked. My plate, which doesn't come with mac salad, has pieces of mac salad here and there. My rice, some of it was so hard and formed little ball-like chunks. My sister's plate, she found a single hair mixed into her tossed green salad. OK, she tries to look past it and enjoy her food. My nephew, he has pork pieces placed underneath his CHICKEN katsu?! Say what?! Chicken katsu doesn't include any pork! My hubby, although his BBQ mixed plate isn't exact of Hawaii's own plate, he still tries to enjoy it. Okay, that's just way too much! I keep moving my pieces of pork around on my plate asking if it is cooked. My awesome hubby gets up to call one of the girls over, he quietly, without making a scene, begins to tell her of the many issues with our orders. we figured, if this was an isolated incident, no need for others to overhear and think twice about their food. Again, this girl is a champ! No hesitation, she apologizes and offers a refund. Okay, I'll accept that. We tell her we witnessed the confrontation earlier with the cook and that we we're sorry for her to have to deal with that. We also let her know L&L in Hawaii was of much higher quality than this. And unfortunately, we will most likely never return to this L&L ever again. This is not about bashing L&L or it's employees. While the cook might need some replacing, those girls are friendly and know good customer service. Its very unfortunate that as a customer, we are subjected to the poor leadership of a company. It's the few bad apples that can bring down the entire reputation of a business. I DO hope the owners of this L&L location are awakened to the fact that they need better leadership for their employees. And, if you're looking for good ono plate lunches, sadly, there's none to be found here.
label: NEG

text: Came here for a celebratory homecoming dinner after my main squeeze had been overseas for two months, and it was a great choice! When you pull in you will be required to valet your car. Notice all the Maseratis, Porsches, BMWs, and Mercedes' flanking the entrance to the restaurant. If you drive a crappy VW like me, it will be hidden way in the back so as not to scar the delicate eyeballs of Mainline 1%ers. The valet is gratis, though, so that's a plus! They were also very fast when retrieving my car at the end of the evening. Noise level was deafening upon entry for an 8pm reservation, but had simmered down a bit by the end of our meal. Dress code was not as formal as the vehicular lineup and valet theatrics would indicate. It was as though everyone was on the same mailing list that informs wealthy white people of what to wear and when, which must also be the medium by which all Mainline housewives know just the right level of upscale athleisure and gold accessories that is appropriate for an afternoon grocery run. Lots of very tan people in the 40s-early 60s age range. The few people I saw closer to our age were with groups that appeared to include their parents. OK, you're reading this for the food, not my snarky classist commentary. We decided to start by sharing a seafood bento and crispy octopus salad. The presentation of the octopus was lovely - it arrived in a covered dish and when the lid was removed with a flourish, bonito flakes danced a delicate, wavy jig on top of the crispy octopus. This dish was excellent and got F's vote for best dish of the night. The seafood bento was also very good - each component included thoughtful accompaniments that were much more than a typical afterthought garnish. Only the shrimp spring roll stood out as rather pedestrian, though not bad by any means, while everything else was spectacular. The tuna tartare in the bento was my favourite item of the night. We moved on to share two specialty sushi rolls, which are quite large. The seared tuna was very good, but didn't stand out as anything really special or unusual to justify the price tag. If it had incorporated a yuzu vinaigrette drizzle or something else to brighten it up I think I would have been more wowed. The King Kong roll was better in theory than in practice. The overall impression was a bit dry, and I'm personally not huge on shishito leaf so that's just my own taste. The end pieces were so huge there was no way to eat them whole, so I pulled out the meats to eat on their own. I found that the beef was incredibly good and it seemed sort of a crime to hide it in a roll like that. A bit gimmicky, and not terribly successful. Finally we each concluded with our own dessert, always the highlight of the meal for F. He got the chocolate torte and I went with the deconstructed s'more. His torte was very good, rich and beautifully presented but not unique or particularly interesting. My s'more suffered the same fate nearly every Top Chef contestant meets in the "deconstruct a dish" challenge. Each component was good on its own, but did not come together in a single bite to evoke the flavour of a s'more. It was also a little confused, with peanut butter and banana being brought to the party. The chocolate peanut butter brulee was interesting but lacked the smooth creaminess of a traditional creme brulee; the banana marshmallows didn't taste much like banana but the torched exteriors were very satisfying; the banana ice cream could have been creamier (it was icy, more like a sorbet) and the graham cracker cake's texture did not play well with the other components, while tasty on its own. To accompany this feast I got a thyme and cucumber gin cocktail that was truly excellent, well balanced with good flavour. In fact, it was so good I decided to get two even though I was planning to only have one, but was then disappointed when my second drink arrived tasting significantly different from the first - sweeter, and less balanced. It was still fine and I drank it, but it speaks to an inconsistent regime behind the bar. The bill was actually not that shocking, especially by Center City standards. Total before tax and tip was about $122, which I found fairly reasonable. Service was good and overall we really enjoyed our experience. We plan to come back in the future for drinks and a full table of appetizers - those were the real stars of the menu and could easily make a meal. We found what we had ordered to be the perfect amount of food, we left full but not stuffed.
label: POS

text: This hotel serves a very curious purpose. To start with the rooms, they are very dated. The furniture is worn and tired and the mattress is lumpy foam. The pillows are very flat and even stacking two pillows isn't comfortable. The windows are dirty and the bathrooms don't have room to turn around in. If you are on a bottom floor like we were (#1112), expect to hear a TON of noise from your upstairs neighbors. Pray yours go to bed early, ours didn't and the thumping and pounding from the ceiling went clear past mid-night and started at 6am again every morning. The manager did respond to our 3rd complaint and spoke with the guests directly. Breakfast: a usual perk of staying at a Marriott was one of the worst I have seen. Every day there is little to nothing remaining when we arrived They don't seem to restock when things run out (eggs, english muffins, yogurt etc) and the bananas put out were literally brown for 3 days before anyone thought to throw them out. On the weekends, the breakfast area is so small it was a mad house and there was no where to sit. For 48+ hours as well, there was no internet. They apparently did some kind of upgrade, but it resulted in no service what-so-ever in the property for over 2 days and on a third day, the service was down completely for another reason. Between the horrible breakfast and the lack of wifi - there's no reason they should charge over $100 a night. Like another review mentioned, the hotel is right off a main road and there is very little option to secure any of your valuables. Housekeeping didn't come for 2 days to our room and we had to call the front desk to get service. After bringing up some of these issues to Management, they did their best to correct them, but substandard service deserves substandard prices. They must be catering to a certain traveler but I am not sure who. Pets: We travel with our dog frequently. The $100 pet charge seems standard at Residence Inn properties (when not waived as a courtesy) but this property also taxes their own pet charge, so expect to pay $108. The service charge doesn't imply additional pet services however, since dog waste was littered throughout the property and was never removed by any of the grounds crew during our 10 day stay and there were no bags in the dog waste area to promote responsible dog clean up. If I needed to stay in the area again, I would not stay at this property. There are far too many options to be corralled into this Residence Inn. I do feel like Management is responsive when they can be, but this property had a lot to be desired.
label: NEG

text: I had an overall fine experience with Stadium Toyota. Not to say that I wouldn't have shopped around a little bit more as any American should, but they were the only dealership in a 100 mile radius that had the vehicle I was looking for, a slightly used Tacoma 4x4 double cab. For some reason there are a lot more 4x2 Tacomas out there than really need to be. Perhaps it is due to the overwhelming public opinion that a 4x4 Tacoma Double cab is probably the most useful truck on the planet and people aren't letting them go. Pricey, but worth it. But that isn't Stadium Toyota's fault, it's the resale value of an unstoppable product. I am willing to bear the expense for the reward of a truck that I know will last me a lifetime. I still have a 1989 4Runner project that was my mothers truck since new, it still runs great today with 250k miles on the original drive train, I'm working on the body now since it was a Missouri truck and had some road salt intrusion. My wife drives our children around in a 2011 Sienna van that we drive all over the country with absolutely zero problems to date. But I digress, Andrew Jernigan, my sales associate, with the aid of Katie the customer concierge, and James Hammons the internet director, were able to get me into the truck I wanted with no hassle what-so- ever. Andrew even gave me his own coffee (that he hadn't drank from yet) right off his desk since I showed up right at opening time. He is a real dude and not some cracked up predatory salesman trying to make a quota. Just a man making a living selling by far the best product money can buy at the best value he can manage. Keith Harrington, the business manager was FAST, even for a Sunday when the credit agencies aren't responding as quick. The deal we made was just .6% APR higher than the current APR I had with my Ford (a mistake I will never make again), but that was only because this Tacoma is a 2008 model and not a 2013 or later, and my wife didn't co-sign with me this time. At 3.5 I can't really complain too much. So, in short, I don't like any BS, and Andrew and his crew didn't deliver any. I am pleased with my purchase and with Stadium Toyota for their professionalism and promptness, and I would definitely recommend Stadium Toyota, their product, and Andrew Jernigan + crew to anyone 1000 times.

text: This outfit is a nightmare. If I could give less than one star I would. Our dishwasher quit working. Never had issues with appliances I called our contractor and they recommended J&B. I always look at Yelp and BBB before using anyones services so I had seen the bad Yelp reviews and there were closed BBB issues. At that point, I had a bad feeling but thought all would work out since recommended and I was desperate to get dishwasher working. I called to make appointment (4 days out), which I was okay with. The day prior to appointment I was called and told the time frame. The technician arrived within time block. Explained the problem and was some motor for something or another. Technician would order part (4-5 days), call with estimate repair price (which he did not) and when part arrived they would call to schedule us for return visit. Since it takes at least 4 days for appointment I did not want to wait till part arrived to schedule. The following day I called and spoke with a young man who agreed that I should schedule now instead of waiting. Scheduled for 5 days out and would be called the day before with window. The day of appointment time block passed and repairman showed up at 6:00pm. Still okay as I know things happen. Took him forever to pull out dishwasher and replace motor. At least 2 hours from start to finish. Then as luck would have it the replacement motor was bad - so loud. Still okay as I know these things happen and not technicians fault. The next day I called for return visit and they wanted to schedule me 2 weeks out. Absolutely not and I insisted for earlier appointment which ended up 5 days later. By now it has been about 3 weeks since initial call. A few days ahead I called to make sure still on and they said yes and I would be called the day prior. The day prior I called to see what time and I was no longer on list - moved to appointment about two weeks out. Apparently, the scheduler did not check on parts before scheduling. They finally worked me in for the next day. Well, the arrival time block comes and goes. Still trying to stay positive until 9:00pm when no one has showed or call. No one called the next day to reschedule or even the following week and at this point I had lost all confidence in their service and really did not want them working on appliances. So I called ATS (Authorized Technical Services) had appointment the 4th day and 2 days later dishwasher working perfectly, didn't even need to pull out dishwasher! Plus only took ATS 30 min. from start to finish - see separate review for ATS. Apparently, J&B technician did not know what he was doing. The cost of ATS was only $20 more than what J&B finally quoted me. Lack of technician knowledge, customer service and follow-up with this outfit....DO NOT USE. text: This is a 2 part review. Firstly I will review a trip one Sunday Mid-2014 to dine in. My son and I went in and feasted on several items. We started with fried pickle spears, fish spread and 2 soups. The spread tasted ok but wasn't homemade like we anticipated from the decor and vibe of the place. The pickles and accompanying sauce were outstanding. The "3 pepper crab" soup was lacking any rustic qualities and was mostly just weird. Very little, low-quality crab sat in a gloopy mess that I strived to taste one of the mentioned 3 peppers in. The "New England clam chowder" was just not good. It is yellow. It's made with chicken soup base. In fact so was the "3 pepper crab". This is a definite no-no for a "Florida cracker" types seafood house. We also ordered a platter with several fried seafood items which was good. Not excellent but not bad either. The shrimp were sweet but a little mushy. The fish was firm and flaky and cooked to perfection. The scallops were out of this world. In fact I spoke of the scallops to anyone who would listen for weeks. The service earned a 30% tip that day. We looked forward to returning. So we did. Only this time he is a bit older and into kids cooking shows and wanted to get some fresh Florida fish. We waited as another customer ordered and I looked over their prices and noticed no fresh fish just big chest-freezers. When it was my turn I asked if all the fish were frozen and was met with a term that is becoming increasingly common, "no it's all 'fresh-frozen'". The owner said this mess of an oxymoron so soft and quickly so as to render it a one word mumble. He obviously knew the implications of it. I said "so it's all frozen then?" and emphasized "frozen" a touch. He asked what I wanted and I explained my son amd I wanted some locally caught fresh, never frozen, wild fish that woukd be good for direct grilling or planking and he told me all his fish were caught in the Gulf and frozen on the boat to which I explained I understood the common practice but was really looking for something else and said "thank you" politely. As I turned and walked away he said in a derisive tone "Hey buddy lemme ask you a question? Where ya gonna buy fresh fish from? It doesn't exist." I turned to explain he need not be rude or insulting, as his tone implied, and that I agreed there were less options available than in years past and it was good to know he wasn't on the short list of where I'd spend my money. He again told me how it didn't exist. So I went to a local seafood shop on the sponge docks as well as Whole Foods Market who both had great selections of never frozen fish whose flesh were still firm and didn't smell. Obviously there is still a small market for the way stuff used to be done. It is a shame the owner of The Fish Guy could not be part of that. I've given it 2 stars because as far as retaurants go they are a 3 star place. Just avoid the soups if you have functional tastebuds. The service, fried seafood and pickles were slightly above average for local fare. However as a market I feel they earn 1 star. There is nothing at all special you won't find at the frozen section of your grocer of choice. They do have things like sauces and spreads that grocers dont carry but they don't seem of high enough quality to warrant a visit or boost the overall star rating.

text: Continuing from Nashville Resident review - cranes taking over parking lots, so there is nowhere to park. Seriously, that's another huge issue all on it's own - parking! Or actually lack thereof. Unless you're going to pay for a parking spot, which you can't even actually buy at the moment, supposedly there is a waiting list, however those spots are currently being used by construction people working on a building, so basically you're fresh out of luck. So...where do you park? Wherever you can! A parking lot is worth gold around here. There is a very small lot in the back, if by some miracle you're able to get that spot, you're good, otherwise, put aside a lot of $ for parking tickets, because brace yourself - you'll be getting a lot of them! Most people park by the meters, some are 7am or tow away spots, some are 8am or get a ticket, and some are 10am or get a ticket. So, if you decide to take a day off during a week, and you didn't get the coveted spot in the back, you'll be parking by the meter, which you have to come down and feed every hour all day or...probably will be less hassle and actually cheaper is getting a parking ticket. Also, consider the fact that there is a Municipal Auditorium right up front of the building, so if there is some sort of an event going on, the city blocks off all the metered spots for the staff working the event for several days at a time, which of course takes away the parking spots from the residents living here. We used to have a parking lot in the front, but since the building is being remodeled and painted that is now closed....indefinitely.....the most absurd thing is that there is nothing going on in the front, there is no reason to take away that many spots from us for months, but it's happening nonetheless. Because the most disturbing thing is that the apartment management could care less about the comfort of the residents, there is absolutely no consideration or any human factor for that matter. There is nothing constant with them, things change from week to week without any of our knowledge. For instance, I was waiting on a package, remembering that they posted new hours of operation on their door, they were going to start working on weekends, so I was thinking that I would be able to get my package without any problems. However, when I got the note on my mailbox that the package has been delivered, I discovered that the office is no longer open on the weekends, so had to wait until Monday to pick up my packages. Online it still listed the old house of operation, the paper with hours was removed from the door, when I called to ask them about it, they said that they can't lease out enough apartments, so it doesn't make sense for them to work on the weekends. Of course! Why should they let the residents who actually live here know anything of the sort! Let them figure it out on their own. It's not just one thing, it's many, many, many things compiled over time. Bottom line is that this place no longer feels like home. Not only that, it feels like the end of my lease date can't come soon enough! I am so tired of something different every week and every time the change is not for the better, executed poorly and not at all in mind with the convenience for the residents. Save your money and your SANITY! Find something else, anything else will be better than this.

text: It is very rare that you get to write a review of an institution that has actually saved your life. At the age of thirteen I was diagnosed with a brain tumor and underwent brain surgery at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. The hospital has won many awards and accolades since its establishment, and I personally never received anything but the best of care while a patient. CHOP, as its more commonly known, admits more than 15,000 children each year; if the President's children were sick, they would probably be patients at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. If nothing else, I'm grateful my parents were able to get me the best medical attention possible. There is no doubt in my mind that a lesser hospital, employing less skilled surgeons, would have left me severely brain damaged, or worse. Once arriving at CHOP, my parents, grief-stricken upon learning of my diagnoses, immediately calmed down. The doctors and nurses had a great bedside manner, the perfect mixture of comfort and professionalism. I remember very little from the day of my surgery. An IV was stuck into my arm and an anesthesiologist sedated me. My neurosurgeon was Doctor Suttor, chief of the neurosurgery division at CHOP. I regained consciousness a few hours later, back in my hospital room. The surgery was a success. When I woke back up I wanted nothing more than a cool drink of water. The doctors forbid me from drinking liquids and I had to be content with ice chips. My head pounded and my hair had been shaved during the surgery. There were twenty staples in the back of my head and all of them itched like hell. After the surgery, I couldn't control the entire right side of my body. It was almost as if I had a stroke, except my right arm and leg shook constantly and uncontrollably. There were bed rails on either side of the hospital bed, as if I were a toddler who just graduated from his crib. It's not easy to get much sleep while you're in a hospital. As tired as I was, I couldn't get any rest. During those few times I was able to fall asleep naturally I would soon be woken up. A nurse would barge into my room, stick me with a needle, and shine a light in my eyes. In the days that followed I regained some control over the right side of my body. My limbs still shook constantly, but now I was able do things like hold a pencil or stand up while leaning against something for support. A physical therapist came by one day and I took my first steps outside the hospital room. My tumor was located in the cerebellum--the part of your brain that controls balance and motor skills, among other things. During such an invasive surgery there's bound to be some brain damage. It's no surprise that I was having trouble with walking and coordination. Immediately after the surgery, there was also concern I'd suffer from memory loss--the cerebellum also controls some cognitive functioning, like attention and memory. Fortunately, I was untouched mentally, but trapped inside a body my brain could no longer control. I was only able to walk on my own by using a gait belt to help with balance. Even then, I couldn't take more than ten steps at a time. A doctor came into the hospital room one day and handed me a plastic medical bag. Inside the hermetically sealed bag was the tumor they cut out of my head. My tumor was the size of a golf ball and pink like a wad of bubble gum. It felt empowering to hold in my hand what had once tried to kill me. I was able to hold down Italian water ice, but little else. I remember trying to eat an orange and vomiting all over myself after the first bite. I can't speak to the quality of hospital food, as even the smell turned my stomach. There was a bootlegger outside the hospital who sold VHS copies of movies still in their theatrical run, or not yet released on home video. My parents bought me a few tapes to play on the VCR in my hospital room. I think Titanic was the first movie I watched after the surgery. I could only handle watching television in fifteen-minute increments, so it took a long time before I finished the entire three-hour movie. There was a McDonald's in the basement of CHOP. I never understood why they let the world's unhealthiest fast food restaurant open up a location in a hospital; maybe they thought sick children wouldn't feel so bad if they were eating a happy meal. On my last day in the hospital I ordered a sausage and egg McMuffin with cheese. I ate the breakfast sandwich, a side of hash browns, and was able to keep everything down. It was a personal triumph. If I was able to handle the greasiest food in the world, there was a chance I wouldn't starve and waste away. All told, I spent a total of two weeks in the hospital. I was given the option of staying at CHOP and continuing my physical therapy there, but I opted to go back home and receive treatment at a local facility.

text: I have a little bit of a food truck fetish. I don't know what it is, but serve food out of a colorfully-painted vehicle and I'm automatically intrigued. I, like many of the other reviewers, also am a Polish girl, raised on home-made pierogi made by my mother and grandmother for the holidays, or someone else's Polish-speaking grandmother for the local church fundraising bazaars. So I do not say this lightly: Mom-Mom's is one of my all-time favorite food trucks, and their pierogi are phenomenal. I was at first turned-off by the concept of pan-seared pierogi. I'd always boiled/steamed them and drowned them in butter, but turns out there is more than one way to make little potato dumplings delicious. The caramelized onion, scallions, and sour cream are the perfect accompaniment to these pockets of heaven. Served up in an unassuming little paper bowl for $8 a serving, they're by far one of the best food-truck deals one can find, and they come with bonus nostalgia (for some, anyway...) My only complaint is that it can be difficult to track them down --- I don't live in Philadelphia, and they don't always widely publicize where they are going to be, so it can be tough to make the trip when they last-minute post on Facebook that they're in a certain park for a few hours. But they are always so, SO worth the trip.
label: POS

text: What a wonderful way to spend a morning! My husband and I took the Mississippi River Tour with Richie--we had a great time. If you can book only one tour while in town, do it here. The leisurely 7-8 mile ride is just as promised by the company--it starts with a few stops in Louis Armstrong Park and a quick stop outside St Louis 1 cemetary, then winds through Treme, the French Quarter and along the NO side of the river front. You get to take a quick ferry ride across the river to the quaint town of Algiers. Here you get to stop for refreshment (alcoholic or non ... We chose the latter) and a chat with your very friendly tour guide. The ride atop the levee back to the ferry (with a quick stop to say "hi!" to a pet turkey) was the highlight for me. After the return ferry trip, it's sadly time to head back to the shop. In sum, if you book with Crescent City Bike Tours (and you should ... like, right now) expect friendly guides, an easy ride on a comfortable cruiser bike and fascinating bits of history and trivia about one very unique city. This particular dinner was meant to be a celebration of graduating medical school. We originally wanted to go to Peche but they were unable to accommodate us as we were a rather large party (14). They recommended we try their sister restaurant Herbsaint. The biggest faux pas of the evening, and what in my opinion is unforgivable, was that 2/4 of the black drum entrees were heinously undercooked. This is not a fish where a little raw in the middle is ok. The fish was not served with any vegetables or accoutrement. It was literally just a bland, baked, piece of drum with a side of pureed (mashed) potatoes that were cold. The rest of the entrees were alright but nothing to write home about. The only thing that was decent was the teres minor and french fries, so if you do make the mistake of wandering into this god forsaken establishment, order that. The service was average at best with the waiter acting somewhere between ambivalent and annoyed. The meals were pricey and unimaginative. In the ever changing restaurant ecosystem that is New Orleans I hope that natural selection takes it's course and that Herbsaint is rapidly made extinct.

The nuts and hummus were a nice combination, but there was nothing complex or special about the flavor. It was as if I had gotten hummus from a nice grocery store, spread it on a toasted whole wheat crust and chopped up some almonds on top. As a result, the pizza as a whole was pretty dry; some other reviews have photos of hummus pizza with olive oil on top, so maybe that's what I was missing. Together, my pizza had the combined flavor of, well, hummus and bread with occasional bites of nuts. I took some of my little brother's cheese pizza because it was warmer and more savory than mine, and it was also just ok. As comparison, I bought myself a three cheese thin crust pizza the other night and baked it in the oven for 15 minutes and ate it. When I think back on that pizza vs the one my brother had, I vastly preferred the boxed to the one from Bella. For example, on one occasion I had asked if the teller could pass me the bags that she had piled my groceries on top of, on the opposite conveyor, as I was stuck in the line blocked by carts, and simply wanted to get a start on bagging...she quite frankly said, "no, I cannot". Another occasion, I had paid and was bagging my items, and I couldn't reach the items left on the counter and not on the belt, so I asked her to push them on to the belt so I could press the button to make the belt move towards me, she decided to ignore me, turned her back to me and leaned on the counter. I am not a rude person, I was very polite and smiled and say hello etc. and felt a pang of embarrassment and could not understand what I had done to make the staff not want to assist me. There are some tellers who are wonderful, if I am lucky enough to shop on a day when they are working, I go to them. text: I never thought I'd be writing a review of a funeral home, but I want people to know about my experience. My parents were kind and smart enough to make advance arrangements with Memorial Park many years ago. Even in that situation, planning for a funeral is a difficult and emotional task. The folks at Memorial Park understand this and were a total blessing to us. When my mother passed away, I called around 5:30 on a Friday, thinking no one would be there and that I'd have to try again on Monday. I left a message and, within a few minutes, Eric returned my call. He was kind, professional and compassionate. He took some information about my mom and let me know that her body was in their care. They use that word a lot - care - and it's appropriate, because I and my family received the best of care from them from start to finish. We provided preliminary information to Eric and made an appointment for Saturday to come in, sign papers, and make decisions and arrangements When you walk into the office at Memorial Park, you will always be greeted by someone who is very professional and courteous. They will offer you water, snacks and a comfortable seat before showing you to a consultation room. Melanie and Kristen were our primary points of contact, but over the course of weeks, I worked with many people, and they were all absolutely fantastic. Melanie was our funeral director, so she helped us take care of arrangements for mom's cremation (paperwork, etc), getting death certificates, and helping us arrange the memorial service. She was responsive (even returning emails on her days off) and delightful to work with. My mom wasn't affiliated with a church, so we used the facilities at Memorial Park for her service and a reception. The facilities are beautiful. When I arrived on the day of mom's service (we brought our own food in for the reception, but you can have caterers deliver food and drink as well), the chapel was already set up. Flowers had been placed, a guestbook and prayer cards were there. Georgia Devero set up/break down the reception room, and she was a blessing, attending to every detail. Rachel Troutt was the funeral director who was on duty when we had mom's service, and she was amazing as well. Attentive to every need, on top of every minor detail. Two older gentlemen - Roger and Frank - were also there to assist and did a fantastic job attending to anything and everything we needed plus acting basically as ushers for the service. The facility has audio/visual capabilities, and we developed a DVD with a slide show of pictures coordinated with music. Rachel did a great job executing on that portion of the service, queueing up everything perfectly. We had also set up photos and albums of mom in the back of the chapel for people to look at as they came in and left. While we were receiving attendees in the reception room, Roger and Frank took everything down and packed it carefully away for us in bags to help make it easier for us to take everything home when we left. They even helped move the flowers from the service over to my parents' niche after the service, carrying a big wreath of flowers on a brutally hot August day. When my mother's remains were ready, we scheduled an internment service to place them in the niche my parents bought, where my dad's ashes were already laid to rest. Again, Kristin and Rachel were on-hand to help. It was raining cats and dogs, and when we got there, they had everything set up in a place indoors where we could say a few words and not get wet. They even had a cooler of bottled water for us. After the ceremony, we needed to take the ashes over to the niche, and it was still storming outside. Rather than have us all get wet, Rachel and Kristen walked back to the funeral home and brought back umbrellas for everyone so we could walk to the niche without getting wet. I could go on and on about these folks. Every single person we came in contact with was absolutely professional, helpful and compassionate. I can't imagine that their jobs are easy but they do a great job. They are also very tightly integrated. Each person has a different function and sometimes they cover for each other, but they never once dropped the ball. I must also mention that funeral homes sometimes have a reputation for trying to sell you things you don't need/want and trying to take advantage of you during an emotionally vulnerable time. At no time did that happen with Memorial Park. While we had plans in advance, they still could have upsold us on things but never did. They laid out options, let us make choices and answered questions helpfully and honestly, even giving us tips to save on the few costs not covered by my parents' plans. They made the worst experience of my life bearable, helped me when I needed it, and gave me things I didn't know I needed to make it easier. I consider them a true blessing. Thank you, Memorial Park and bless you all!

I liked them on facebook immediately, and saw where now starting today they have an area baker who is going to be supplying cinnamon rolls and other bakery items - and I cannot wait to go back. I'm giving this two stars because four days later, now that the inflammation has finally worn down, it looks like my technician did a decent job. text: I'm not even sure where to begin, but I'm going to anyways. As sandwiches go, no one can touch this place, I mean no one! That is not just because it is a deli that also serves beer. On a quick aside, I'd be, oh so happy if they put Guinness back on one of the taps, but I completely understand why it isn't; I won't be a hater and recognize, I am Guinness elite. Having got that out of the way let's just say, the deli that serves beer on tap makes me a happy guy, and the choices are pretty dang good. The staff is great, they are always so friendly, polite, accommodating, and on a few trips the owner (I'm fairly sure he is the owner) was here and also equally cordial. More than cordial, he was gracious. On to the sandwiches: for the record they are amazing! I almost don't even know where to begin; guess I'll break it down. Today's trip was the Dark Bite and wow! Layers of flavor, sweet, then succulent pastrami, cream cheese, then jalapeños, then the onion, and it is just waves of flavor in your face until you swallow, and then standby for the next wave of flavors. It is just waves of deliciousness punching you right in the tastebuds. Ask for it in a roll, but unless you have a big appetite, bring a partner, otherwise be warned: it is a lot to eat, and comes in only one size. On to the rest of the food, it is all so dang good. Several to choose from and they make sandwich science here. The bread is so fresh and simply amazing. The sandwiches are overstuffed and beautifully prepared. The meat is all top notch and the ingredients fresh. I am a huge pastrami fan so it's not a stretch for me to enjoy it as part of my meal, but my wife who's not a fan of the cured delicious meat even likes Beach Hut's pastrami (and she can really be the picky one). To wrap it up, you just can't go wrong here, it is all, oh so incredibly good. Great location ('cause it's close to my home), great beer selection (and they serve beer in the first place), and great sandwiches made with fresh tasty ingredients. Almost forgot, they've got 80's arcade games that are mostly in great shape, and does it get any cooler than that? No, it's not COD, but I'm a Galaga, Ms. PacMan guy anyway.

Within minutes our waiter came with wine glasses for our bottle of wine, warm bread and explained the tasting menu. The food parade of small tapas followed shortly after, and I want to say continued in nice timing for about 60/ 70 minutes. The samplings were primarily of smaller tapa style samplings, but plenty, as I believe we sampled at least 6 plates. All of which were well prepared. Everything was tasty and embodied the traditional flavors that comes with Greek cuisine. No fancy presentations, yet excellent executed dishes with traditional flavors! We were satisfied enough to not need anything else to eat, yet we found room for dessert and traditional coffee. Glad we did, because it was excellent and the perfect ending to a great food layout. The staff was very attentive, but not overbearing in way that interrupted our table's conversation. Nice flow, nice service. Great for dates. Great for a Sunday supper/ Sunday dinner with an old friend or a small intimate group. I certainly will be returning.

text: I recently visited my friends in Idaho and this was on the list of places I "had to see". The place: I was told this place was an underground bar/arcade. Now mix it with a bar and you have winning, or so i thought.... My friend and I showed up to find the place indeed underground and with a bar, but not exactly as I expected. Well, not at all like I expected. The place is small and cramped, as if someone took a basement and placed a small bar then shoved some very old arcade games to the side and said "Grand opening!" To put things in perspective, picture walking into a very crowded room. To your left all along the wall, you see pinball machines (about 10 or so). In front and to the right you see a row of arcade machines, not the kind found in an arcade nowadays, but rather ones found in your parents days and old 80's movies. You know, the old ones with a screen and levers (joysticks), like Donkey Kong. Now imagine walking forward, but dough, you just bumped into someone cause the isle isn't wide enough for both of you. But you maneuver your way through and to the right, right to the "bar area". To your right you see a small bar and in front you see a few tables (all taken by young drunks). You decide to turn around play some games instead, but find there's maybe 1 arcade game open and no pinball machines open. What do you do? That's exactly what happened for me. This place has the potential to be great. To be exactly what I first pictured. Maybe if they found a bigger place and expanded their game choices it'd be a grand place, but as of now, it's simply too cramped and has far to few games I've even heard of, let alone know how to play, for it to be any place I'd visit again.

text: So I really wanted to like this place. Nice, open atmosphere. Freshly baked scones with delicious clotted cream and the Americano was superb - all at a reasonable price. AND they accept credit cards with a reliable wifi! As a grad student who gets the most work done at cafes early in the mornings, Steap and Grind appeared to be an awesome find. I came here around 8am on a weekday to get some work done. There was no one at the counter, but I saw that there was one patron sitting and getting some work done so I thought the barista must have just gone to the bathroom or something. Eventually, he came out (I waited probably about 5 minutes), took my order. Mediocre service - definitely not anywhere near rude, but mediocre. My multiple "thank yous" were returned with no response. But I am not the type to be picky about mediocre service - and the scone and coffee were enough for me to forget about the mediocre service. I plopped down to do some work, and this is where things got a little funny for me. I saw that the same barista who had given me mediocre service was giving SUPERB service to everyone who walked in the door. I heard him say multiple times - "No, thank YOU" to customers' "thank yous." I sat there for 2 hours to do work, and he made sure to go out of his way to say "Thank you" and "Goodbye" and "have a good one!" to everyone who left the cafe. Again, something small I noticed, but shrugged off. It's not that big of a deal. Maybe he just needed time to wake up. About an hour and a half into my work, the same barista came around and asked everyone around me if he could take their plate but blatantly skipped me. My plate was empty. He asked if he could take the plate to the customer next to me who still had some of her pastry left. And then he went onto ask the customer on the other side of me. I was preparing to give him my plate had he not skipped me. At this point, I felt like there was some sort of discrimination in his service, but again, maybe it's just coincidence. I put my plate and coffee cup away - he looked up to see me pack up and get up - and then walked out the door to no "have a good day" or "good bye" or "thank you". I had sat there for 2 hours listening to him be overly chipper and friendly to everyone else. Seriously, this doesn't sound like the biggest deal (and it really isn't). I am ok with mediocre service as long as the mediocre service is equal. I really dislike it when people play the race card but it is true that I was the only minority customer who had walked in the time frame that I was sitting in the cafe. Other plausible explanations for his discriminatory behavior toward me: - I probably looked the youngest out of everyone else there (although I probably wasn't) - Maybe I looked like his ex-girlfriend? - Maybe I reminded him of a customer who gave him a hard time - Maybe he doesn't like people wearing blue skirts (I was the only one in a blue skirt) Regardless. It left a bad taste in my mouth, which is a shame because the scone and the coffee left my taste buds wanting for more. It is very plausible that today was just an off-day. But my experience there was uncomfortable enough that I will be taking my business elsewhere.

text: My husband and I were on a road trip through NOLA looking for a good place to try crawfish boil and/or jambalaya. We picked this place because it was near our hotel (walking distance), on the famous Bourbon street, and had good reviews on yelp. I honestly have no idea how this place had good reviews on yelp. We started by ordering something previous reviewers recommended: sautéed crab claws. If it weren't for this appetizer, I would have rated the restaurant one star instead of two. The claws had very sloppy and poor presentation and was almost no food for $13. If you google image search sautéed crab claws before hand, just know that that's nowhere near what you will get. Picture something closer to a shallow bowl of soup with a few floating crab claw tips in it. The taste of it was the only thing that saved it at all, but even then it was only slightly above average. When my husband went to order the crawfish boil, which was basically starred and bolded on the menu, he was told it was "out of season" and wouldn't be available again until next summer. Maybe our fault for not doing the research ahead of time (? If it is even true?) but still a big letdown. So he went with the waiter's recommendation of the Cajun Trio. I ordered the blackened shrimp with jambalaya and steamed vegetables. What I was not expecting is frozen veggie medley (you know, the really cheap grocery store kind with peas, tiny carrot cubes, and corn) barely warmed and tossed onto the plate. If you are going to serve me 25 cent vegetables, at least try a little harder.. And as for the Jambalaya, you could probably have it with more flavor and texture of you made it from the Uncle Bens boxed mix. It seriously looked like the bad kind of hospital cafeteria food and tasted very bland. The shrimp were far from blackened. Tasted okay, but nothing special for $17. My husbands meal was even more confusing. It was served in three tiny bowls and each looked exactly the same. The server offered to add fried crawfish to the tops to make up for us missing the crawfish boil, but didn't note that it was $5 extra... text: In the interest of disclosure, this restaurant probably deserves 4.5 stars because I've had some pretty mediocre service before. However, I went last night and the service was on point so I bumped it up to five. I went because someone told me they have the best fish and chips in Tucson. It's funny because I've never actually tried the fish and chips, but I haven't gone wrong yet! It's a large, single room pub. Very loud, so you won't want to come if you're looking for a romantic outing. As others have mentioned, lots of military memorabilia everywhere. I like it and I'm happy to support the business of a local Tucson veteran as my husband is also a veteran. I'm impressed at the appeal this place has to a large variety of demographics. I came here one night and felt very out of place because it was loaded with college students (my college days are behind me), but come another night and you'll see mostly folks in their 40s, or groups of older ladies, or groups of veterans, or mid 20s people like me looking for some good food. I like that because it feels very inclusive. Excellent atmosphere to have at a pub and I wonder how they do it - I bet a lot of people would pay the owners for their secrets on how to appeal to everybody like that. I could absolutely see myself becoming a regular here. Now, onto the food, the most important part! The first time I came here I had the Chesapeake Bay burger because I am an Old Bay freak. Big, stuffed with goodies, and excellent flavor. However, they have lighter dishes that will actually appeal to you rather than forcing you to feel like, "Crap, I'm on a diet, I guess I'll have this nasty wilted salad." I came here the other night and wanted to try their famous clam chowder. I had a soup and sandwich combo with the chicken salad sandwich. Now, I still think that my grandma's chowder is better, but I won't say that I didn't enjoy that chowder immensely. At request they top it with a generous bit of bacon and green onions. Yum! The sandwich impressed me a lot as well because you don't see chicken salad everywhere, but it's one of my favorites. It comes on toasted bread with the perfect amount of chicken salad. And it's not an overly sweet salad either. You know I liked it because I came back the next night and had the exact same thing. Ok, so, the service. Last night it was out of the park. Jason noticed me at the door looking for a table and used his immense height to locate one for me in the nearly-full house. He was very pleasant and even checked on me later to see how I was doing. Janelle was my server and she was amazing. I order coffee when I come here rather than a beer because as much as I love beer, I work graveyards and need to wake up before my shift. This usually means that they have to brew a new pot because I don't know who else comes there for coffee at 9pm on a Friday night except me. However, she did so without complaint. She was always prompt and had a smile on her face the whole time. She knew what the soup of the day was without having to go check (other servers at this place sometimes don't...) and I just adored her. Never once felt ignored - and I was a one top taking up a table on a busy night. Thank you, Janelle! As for other service I've had, it would echo what countless other reviewers have mentioned. Young, pretty college girls who have a little trouble paying attention to their tables. Like I said, they often don't know the specials, and you might have to chase them across the restaurant for the check, where you'll probably find them sitting at the bar, chatting with their friends. I don't get worked up about it because I know what restaurant work is like, it can be a grind, and they will go get my check if asked. It is sort of irksome that I have to go find them, though. It's also a little annoying that this is my usual experience with the service here, rather than Janelle the rockstar. A note to the restaurant: if half your yelp reviews echo this experience with the service (which they do), maybe work on a little server training. It's ok to socialize, restaurants are social places, but you also need to do your job while on the clock. Like I said, though, I'm still giving this place five stars because I love it. Come here and you won't be disappointed.
