text: For a special occasion, be sure to get a booth For this visit my wife made reservations for us on open table.com for our 12th wedding anniversary. When we arrived we were greeted by the hostess who took our last name, fiddled around for what seemed like two or three minutes, and then asked us to follow her to our table. We were situated in what was basically the middle of the room on a four top. Before we sat down, my wife and I actually teetered on whether or not we should request a booth or not, but we ultimately remained seated at this table thinking that the restaurant must have been full which is why we ended up with this table. Later we would discover that we were completely incorrect on that assumption and that we could have been given a much more romantic booth. We would also later learn that this restaurant actually has about a dozen secluded booths which we discovered on our way out, poking our heads into different rooms as we made our way to the door. Honestly, I found that to be truly inexcusable as we purposely made the restaurant aware that we were there for our anniversary several times over. We started the evening with the pear and brie cheese fondue and a bottle of the Mirassou Pinot Noir for $30. The wine is a fairly decent bottle which would normally set you back $10 in the store. It has strawberry undertones and we found it to be quite delightful for our meal. The fondue was served with a small bowl of vegetables including mostly cauliflower, followed by celery, and carrots. In another bowl we found Granny Smith apples and lastly a large bowl of sliced bread, which was a mixture of French and a couple of pieces of wheat/French bread. I would suggest asking for just bread during this phase of your meal as the other items do not allow you to actually experience the wonderful blend of cheeses and pears. In fact, I'd venture to say that the vegetables will actually leave you scratching your head as to why they are served in the first place. We decided not to get any salads, and instead move directly to entrées. It is suggested that you get two or three of the entrée choices to make up each individuals meal. While I found this to be spot on in terms of portion size, I do have a few suggestions. My wife and I each ordered filet mignon, and I ordered the lobster tail and my wife ordered the shrimp as our second entrées. I am going to guess that the portion sizes for each plate are around 4 ounces. We both found the fillets to be perfect cuts of meat. The lobster tail was cut into four pieces and was very strangely sprinkled with some sort of red granular spice that neither of us could identify. This seemed to detract from the overall taste of the lobster so much so that for my second piece I actually dumped it in my water glass and swirled it around until most of that "red seasoning" was absent. Then and only then did the lobster actually taste like lobster. Overall for the $9.50 you pay for the lobster tail I'd recommend skipping it. Same was true unfortunately for the shrimp as well. You only get three shrimp for the price, making them difficult to share and they are large shrimp not jumbo, which makes the value poor. It would probably be better to either double up on the filet which was an excellent choice or perhaps grab another protein. We also decided to try the macaroni and cheese and grilled vegetables as a couple of additional sides. The description of the macaroni and cheese sounded delightful and we asked about it with our server he said it was truly incredible. I have a couple of very important suggestion I have regarding side items. First, skip the vegetables as they were just "okay" as a mixture of zucchini, green peppers and string beans, mostly. Next, I would advise that if you do get a side item such as the macaroni and cheese which was incredibly delightful it would be best for you to eat that first as the rest of your meal will wait. We decided to nibble on this along the way and unfortunately about halfway through our entrées we discovered that it got cold a little too quickly and didn't taste as nearly as good at room temperature as it did when it was hot. For dessert we decided on the "Dark and Dulce" and a couple of glasses of Grand Marnier. The dessert was described as "a classic flavor combination featuring our dark chocolate and sweet, thick dulce de leche accented with coarse ground sea salt". It was served with an assortment of side items on one, plate, even though you pay per person. Items included some bananas, strawberries, poundcake, rice crispy treats, blonde and chocolate brownies and dusted marshmallows. Other than the fruit, everything we tried seemed off. I'd swear that the rice crispy treats were actually stale. We ended up asking for additional strawberries and bananas and giving back the entire plate. We were brought out a couple of bowls of strawberries and bananas both of which were quite fresh and delicious. Overall this dessert tasted wonderful

text: I found South Philly Psychic via Yelp and the very helpful review of Vinny L. and with the urging a friend. I've been to a couple psychics before, one at a psychic fair in a nursing home as a high-schooler, where I was told that that summer I would have two boyfriends who would fight over me - not fulfilled! And another in Old City who told me and my two friends that none of the men we were dating were the right ones for us, which given our ages could have been a lucky guess. She also told me that I should return to school to work on my writing because it would prove lucrative. Shout out to that psychic, I'm in debt! I've always felt a little uncomfortable around psychics, kind of like when I go to get my haircut and I want extra attention and advice and they just give me long layers and ask me where I go to school. It's never enough and I always feel like I'm overpaying. I climbed the narrow, steep shag carpeted stairs of South Street Psychic avoiding the piles of catalogs and coupon books sliding down around my feet. A face appeared at the door - almost as if she knew I was coming! "Are you hear for a reading, my dear?" said the woman at the door. We made an appointment for an hour later, and hit the bar in the meantime. Note to future customers: Roxanne has a lot going on, and her business might be a front for something else, so best to book ahead. You think you're the only person in the city who wants to know whether they're going to die alone? When we returned, my friend made me do my reading first. I didn't have enough money for the tarot reading but was stupid enough to get the combination aura and palm reading. Although the space is presented as a storefront, Roxanne performs her services in what appears to be her house, at her kitchen table. I noticed a bag of Friskies Indoor Delights - also my brand! So a point for Roxanne on that front. Roxanne seemed stressed and preoccupied while giving me my reading - after she shut down her game of Candy Crush she checked her text messages at least twice and received a call once. Scrolling through her Twitter feed, she noted that my aura was purple with a little bit of stress clouds hanging around, and that I seemed like a good person and I had good energy - which is the exact thing I'd wanted her to say. She barked at me to put my hands on the table, and after getting up to open the door for the Verizon guy, who then took his place feet away from us in the living room, she said I was going to have more than three children - possibly around four. The specificity of the number was what really got me. She also told me that an old flame would enter my life again soon, but that it wouldn't be good. Someone I regrettably hooked up with three years ago LITERALLY viewed my LinkedIn profile this week, so I'm going to give Roxanne another point for that. My friend's tarot card reading was more extensive. Roxanne told her she was going to have a baby within the next year! Terrifying. As the Verizon guy and I stood in the living room - and I need to say that a point against the space is its total lack of ambience: the ESP Tarot light-up sign piled high with athletic caps and a 12 bottle pack of Mountain Dew, for example - he whispered to me, "If she was really psychic she would know what was wrong with her internet."

text: I scouted out Valley Mount for pasture board for my arthritic 20 year old gelding after a disappointing visit to Kraus Farms next door, thinking it couldn't get any worse. Boy, was I wrong. The woman I spoke to wouldn't let me see the pasture (red flag #1). Then she told me that all the horses are run en masse into metal slat stalls each morning for grain, which isn't measured or monitored to see who's getting what. I didn't see it happen in person, but one can imagine the kicking, fighting free-for-all. Not a good situation unless your horse is an alpha or a youngster who can take the abuse. (red flag #2) "You'll never have to catch your horse at Valley Mount," said the woman proudly, explaining that if I wanted to see my horse on any given day, I'd have to call before noon, and then he would be left in a stall after the morning free-for-all, waiting for me until I came out. What happens if you don't call before noon? Well, you don't see your horse, even though you're the one paying to keep him there. "So it's like he's in jail?" I joked, aghast. (red flag #3) The woman was not amused. But hey, neither was I--maybe I'm old fashioned, but I think that if I'm paying several hundred a month to keep my horse somewhere, I should have free access to him, be able to see where he's being kept, and know the horses he's being kept with. Like Kraus, this place might've been nice 60+ years ago, but it's not for anyone who's serious about their horse's safety and standard of care.

I read that the location was tucked away in a strip mall and a little hard to find, so the tip to look for Gold's Gym was helpful. I just took I-275 to Busch Gardens, turned right on Florida, then right on Waters, and it is on the right before Dale Mabry. The outside of Gio's has an awning and a little bit of outside seating. Once entering, we were greeted, and promptly led to a table. It was lunchtime, and there was only one other table occupied. The dining room is fairly small, but makes good use of the space. There are wine bottles lining the wall, and a piano at the front, which is played on the weekends. The atmosphere felt a little classy actually, with dimmer lighting, a flower on each table, and nice tablecloths. As I always do before going to a restaurant, I checked out the menu online to see what I would order. I had narrowed my choices to two pasta dishes, the Linguini Di Mare (Seafood linguini. Linguini with shrimp, calamari, clams, mussels and scallops in white or red tomato marinara sauce) and the Linguini Alla Vongole (Linguini with clams. Linguini with fresh clams in a red or white wine sauce). However, when I heard one of their specials was lobster ravioli, I promptly changed my mind. While waiting for our entrees we were brought bread and house salads, which come with lunch entrees. The bread was soft thankfully, because I hate getting bread where the crust might break my tooth. The house salad was very good, containing mixed greens, carrots, and their homemade dressing. Additonally, we ordered the Bruschetta Al Pomodoro appetizer (Thinly sliced fresh baguette brushed with olive oils and garlic and topped with fresh chopped tomato and basil). I really liked my lobster ravioli, which was done in their princess sauce, and contained a nice amount of filling. There were five ravioli, which was a good portion for me. My boyfriend ordered the Vitello Millanese (Veal dish. Pounded veal lightly breaded and topped with homemade bruschetta), and came with a side of bowtie pasta. The lunch prices are pretty reasonable, I think our entrees were about $13-$15. We took a peak at the dinner menu, and those items are quite pricey for us (in the $20s). The service was very good, and we had several different people remove finished plates and refill drinks. We will definitely go back for lunch.

text: I've never experienced anything as unbelievable as to what happened at this hotel. I travel regularly as the owner of two companies and this was my first time staying at an Omni Hotel. After a long week of travel, my partner met me to see the gateway arch and explore the city museum, two local attractions. When we got back to our room that night, we were in shock. Our room, 208, was directly above the bar that had music louder than a dance club. This was at 11:30 at night. We decided to relax thinking they certainly could not go past midnight. They did. I called the front desk and they did not answer, probably because they knew why I was calling. I called again and the staff member picked up...you could hear the music clear as day though the handset. I asked her when the music would be shut down as we needed to sleep (It was now 12:05 AM), she told us they were going until 1:00. I asked if there was anything they could do as we were very tired, like move us to a different room, and she said no...but she would leave a note for the manager. We continued to listen to music that was conversation level in our room with lyrics that were derogatory to African Americans and the LGBT community and a song about something called truffle butter that comes from lady parts. We were both in shock that the hotel would allow such explicit music to be played in an open lobby area at 12:30 at night - especially when it could be heard clearly on the 2nd floor. It left us wide awake wondering what they meant by things like truffle butter - quite disturbing as we are a gay couple. Finally at 12:50 they shut down the music, and our room became peaceful - we had no other complaints about the room besides the fact that we could not sleep until 1:00 AM. We were taken aback when in the morning they slipped the hotel bill under our door without even an acknowledgement of what had happened overnight. Surely I thought to myself that the manager at the front desk was ready to rectify the situation. When I went to check out he said the total and told us to have a good day. I told him that we had a terrible night in the room (208) and told him a note was left for the manager to discuss with us in the morning. He told us he was the manager and wasn't aware. We explained what happened and he told us they would take off our parking for the night. That seemed like a pittance given that from 10 PM on most hotels will enforce a noise ordnance and throw guests out that do not comply. Our only option was to lay awake in our bed and listen to the disgusting lyrics in our room, some of which were highly offensive to a gay couple. I told him I would not have paid anything for the room or stayed at the hotel had I known this would have been our experience and he said, "I'm sorry for the inconvenience." We left infuriated at the situation and how poor customer service is at the Omni Majestic Hotel and that they felt free parking justifies keeping guests up until 1:00 AM without any prior notice. Certainly we will never be staying in this hotel again, and it brings into question the Omni brand being that this was our first experience.

text: OK, so I've read the other reviews of this Trader Joe's and I am ready to weigh in. So, I have waited 9 years, 7 months and 2 days for Boise to get a Trader Joe's. What I want to address are the haters who are writting negative reviews. 1st, yes the parking lot is not the best, I go around 10 in the morning and there is NOBODY there, I can park right in front of the store, no problem. I think it doesn't get nasty until after noon or so. I realize that many folks can't shop until after work, BUT, there is a parking garage RIGHT ACROSS THE STREET at BODO. They will carry your groceries to that parking garage and any other for you if you need help, no problem. I have gotten discount coupons for the parking garage also from the front desk when I parked there, you might just have to ask. 2nd, To complain that you have to drive all the way downtown is total crap, seriously, people in the Treasure Valley have no perspective about what real traffic is like or how far one has to drive in larger urban areas. I live in Meridian and it takes me a grand total of 13 mins door to door, big deal. I heard someone complain that they had to drive all the way from Eagle. Really?! If you live in Eagle I'm pretty sure you are use to having to drive a long way for ANYTHING. People, you are spoiled here, and good luck finding organic/non-GMO food for the prices they have at Trader's. I think your savings would off set the price of fuel, which some yelpers complained about. 3rd, I have never had bad service here, on the contrary, the crew members are very helpful and very friendly. To address the complaints that they are always stocking and there are boxes stacked around, I wonder if you have ever been to another Traders because that is the norm, as they want to keep everything as well stocked as they can. This is to deal with all of those who complain if something isn't in stock. I have never had any trouble getting around these, and every other grocer in this town stocks as well, with plenty of boxes to navigate around also. 4th, no, you can't find absolutely everything on your list at Trader's. They carry around 3,000 products. Normal grocery stores can carry up to 50,000. But, what you can get is exceptional, and if you don't like anything for any reason, they will give you your money back if you return the packaging, even if you eat every last bite. In a nutshell, be freakin' happy we finally have a Trader Joe's here and stop complaining about everything.

The important thing you need to know about Asian hair salons is that they give your hair a pre-wash (shampoo and conditioner included) before actually starting to cut your hair. Since I'm not too particular with my hair, I just gave the barber some general guidelines and let him get to work. Once or twice he asked for my feedback, but for the most part he silently snipped and shaved. I could not have been in the chair for longer than fifteen minutes and it was done. I went back for a final wash before the barber made some final touch-ups and threw on some wax for good measure. I didn't even feel the need to ask for an exact quote (men's cuts are $12+), I just handed over $20 because that's what I felt the whole cut and wash was worth. Clean and professional, it's hard to do better than Ben Hair Salon.

text: Average, mediocre, blasé. There are just so many hot chicken joints in Nashville, and you have to be REALLY REALLY GOOD to stand out in this ultra-competitive market! I laugh when my New York friends say "Hot chicken? As opposed to cold chicken?" They just don't get it. Like many locals, I consider myself a hot chicken connoisseur, having sampled everything from the original Prince's to the virtually unknown Deezie's, even braving the roughest neighborhood in New Orleans to try their version of this spicy deep-fried poultry. So please allow me to set you straight. Pepperfire, like Hattie B's, may achieve high marks from tourists who haven't eaten enough hot chicken to make a fair comparison, but both of these restaurants are huge disappointments when you've had the "real thing." The chicken I had at Pepperfire was much like Hattie B's, crispy outside but dry and flavorless inside. And mediocre french fries to boot. Good enough for a Music City visitor ignorant of the rights and wrongs of this gastronomic phenomenon, but not good enough for my discerning palate! If you are a tourist looking for the real deal, PLEASE listen to an expert. If I had one last meal, it would be the absolutely perfect breast quarter (with a side of hot catfish) from Big Shake's in downtown Franklin!!! If they couldn't get that for me, I'd take 400 Degrees or Cool Springs' new Roosters Hot Chicken. The rest aren't really worth the effort.

text: Is it a park, or a beach? I think that is where the confusion is found in the reviews I've seen written up on this ridiculously fantastic hidden gem. First off, let's get one thing straight, Tampa doesn't have beaches, none notable in size or reputation at least. We've got Ben T. Davis on the Causeway, which is a man-made "beach," we've got Picnic Island and then we've Cypress Point. Now, anyone who grew up here is familiar with this spot because it was a classic hideout for High Schoolers to illegally drink. It was just a sandy spot to park at the ass end of some business park off of Cypress. We called it Cypress Point back then, and I've heard it referred to as all kinds of other silly things, but no matter its many names, it was never a nice destination, and you certainly wouldn't take your family out there. Fast forward to 2015. I'm nerding out on Google Maps using the satellite view when I notice lots of cars, people and a clean beach where Cypress Point used to be. And it even looked like there were amenities. Could the city have come in and actually made good use of what could be a nice spot? I had to find out, so off I went. When I arrived, I first couldn't believe I remembered how to get there. I'm getting old, so it was good to see I haven't lost my damn mind yet. Second, I was astonished by the official park-like entrance, well-manicured landscape, trash bins, grills and signage. There were tons of folks out there and kids were frolicking in a playground area. There was a public restroom, and water fountains. It was like being in some parallel Tampa universe. I waltzed over to the benches near the beach, enjoyed the breeze and snapped some pics of the setting sun over Tampa Bay. It was relaxing, and I was just internally excited that this little strip of land had been put to good use. To any newcomers, please think of this as a city park that happens to be on a small stretch of sand on the bay and you won't be disappointed.
label: POS

While we were promptly greeted by the server it was more of "what do you want to drink" and less of "here are some cocktail/beer/wine menus to look over while I grab you some water" No big deal. I asked for menus and we ordered and got our drinks. On the second round we got our wine in snifter glasses, odd but not totally terrible. Funny if anything given that 4 of us ordered wine and on the second round they ran out of glasses...and we were still the only people in the bar. We ordered some apps and asked when the pianist were going on since we had been there 45 mins and nothing was happening (the person that booked the reso was told the start at 5 or 6pm on Saturdays). We were told with a chuckle that no one gets here until 9pm. 40 mins later our apps came and we all ate our fresh from the freezer selection. During all this we were freezing, the ladies had their gloves on and even I was cold (I run hot so that is a rarity). I asked the manager when he came by what the deal was since it was legitimately 50 degrees in the room. He said the heat has been broken since Thursday but don't worry because when more people get here it'll get warmer. Mind you, it was 10 degrees outside. When we left the manager and the hostess were shocked that we'd leave because we were cold. We went over to Misconduct and got warm had great food and drinks, then some folks went back over to this place around midnight. text: After seeing this place listed as the best restaurant in Nashville on TripAdvisor (right behind a pizza place and coffee shop), we made reservations the day of (Friday night) through Open Table while traveling. Other reviews said sometimes you need to book 1-2 weeks in advance, but we were lucky! The atmosphere for dinner is posh, dark, clean, and modern looking. We enjoyed the high-end feel, and my fiancé wore a polo, jeans, and tennis shoes, so it wasn't pretentious. The wait staff was kind and knowledgeable about the food and wine list in great detail and offered amazing recommendations for both! The food was superb: - Pork belly appetizer was so tender it could easily be cut with a fork and melted in your mouth! - The filet mignon was tender (even at medium well) and had amazing, juicy flavors. I'm a steak snob after living in Dallas for years, so I was impressed with this steak! - The fried brussel sprouts side is the way to go if you love brussel sprouts at all! They taste succulent, but without a bunch of fried breading. All sides are meant to be shared with 1-2 other people. The two of us shared one side. We enjoyed the wine recommended to us and appreciated the fact that our waitress suggested a good-priced wine, not the expensive ones. Cabernet bottle prices start at $60-70 a bottle and run much higher! For one appetizer, two meals, one side, and a bottle of wine, we spent $180 before tip. The average dinner plate runs $30, which is a great price for what you get and being so high rated...filets are easily $50 at other steak houses! I highly recommend to anyone staying close to downtown Nashville. It's also a street over from Music Row and all of the action!

We happened to see a physical therapist couple (parents of my child's friend) over the weekend at an event, both of whom looked at my child's leg and recommended we get a referral for PT due to my child's highly awkward gait and overall stiffness. I inquired with GBO on a Monday morning and was told by the front office they would send a referral to the PT office I requested and that I should "work with" my child (try doing amateur PT on your 4-year-old without any formal instruction; it's pretty useless and frustrating for all involved). I was first told the physician was busy in surgery for days and hadn't/couldn't get to it (okay, fine) and that I was told this yesterday (no, I was not; why would I come in again if I was told this?). I was also offered the unsolicited opinion that I would NOT get a PT appointment anywhere that week (because insurance, pre-authorization, etc.). I'm not sure if it was me being pushy or the PT office requesting a referral from GBO, but, after three days, GBO finally sent it. We got an appointment for a PT evaluation the next day because a PT evaluation DOESN'T REQUIRE PRE-AUTHORIZATION. Shouldn't the business side of an orthopaedic office know this, or was this just more BS? I find this sort of behavior is more common in offices that rely mostly on Medicaid patients; as if we'll all just roll over and go away when treated like crap. So, GBO, if you read this, people are pretty understanding if the front office is honest with them. What they don't like (and what leads to a review like this) is condescension and deceit.

Service was quick, the family running the show was friendly. The daughter was working the ovens, the mother was commanding the register and Joey was running the cold side. It was a very well oiled machine. All in all I plan on returning to Joeys for a slice of cheese pizza in the very near future. That being said, my only complaint and the only thing that prevents a 5 star review is the system they have in place for claiming your order. They have an intercom set up and the expo gal will call out the orders over the speakers when they are ready. The problem is that she just calls out vague things like "two slices of cheese pizza" or "slice of pepperoni." Obviously, this is an issue because there are often many similar orders in the dining room and this creates confusion for the guest. I don't think it's entirely too far fetched to arrange a numbered order system to eliminate uncertainty when you go to claim your slice. At any rate, Joeys, I will be back. You are a pleasant establishment in an unexpected location and I appreciate your diligent efforts to produce NY Style all the way down in Nashville.
